prompt: post hoc: written after the compare-v2 run had been scored against these references, to fix quotes that broke the JSON output and rate moves compared by level; its agreement is not an independent estimate
notes: A same gold label does not mean no shift: each statement was labelled on its own text, so two hawkish statements can differ in how hawkish they are (e.g. a hike followed by a hold: both hawkish, and the prompt counts it as a shift), and an analysis that reads such a pair as a shift is not necessarily wrong.

The zero-shot score delta comes from the same model family (llm_zero_shot judging each statement alone): agreement with it is a consistency cross-check, not independent validation. llm_zero_shot is also prompted with the rubric the reference annotators followed, so its delta agrees with the gold-implied shift largely by construction: its baseline rows are an upper-bound cross-check, not a baseline the comparison should beat.

The rate-decision rule (rate_decision_vs_gold, same_label_by_rate_decision) is post hoc: added after the analyses had been scored. It reads each statement's decision on the target range with app.stance.statements.rate_action and compares the two decisions as the prompt's rule 9 does; a statement without a rate decision (2019-10-04, 2020-03-23) gives unchanged in the baseline.

Pairs share statements (each statement is the target of one pair and the base of the next), and the bootstrap resamples pairs as if independent, so the intervals understate the uncertainty; the year-block intervals are a sensitivity check.
confidence is model-reported, never a calibrated probability.

earlier_prompts.prompt: pre-registered: the prompt was fixed before any analysis was scored against a reference
